extracted.intended_audience: legal scholars, public administration researchers, and practitioners interested in administrative law and administrative contracts
extracted.subtask_description: Scholarly analysis of the notion, purpose, and novelty of an administrative contract within the (new) Law on General Administrative Procedures, with comparative reference to European administrative practice and implications for public administration reform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public administration normative goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the premises that public administration should serve as an open, digitally developed and work-transparent public service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This normative statement functions as an evaluative standard for assessing reforms and instruments (like administrative contracts): reforms should advance openness, digital development, and work-transparency in public service delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative contract purpose — meeting citizens' demands
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine and conclude whether this agreement provides an essence of citizens’ social and economic demands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing an administrative contract, assess whether it addresses and embodies citizens' social and economic needs; the paper uses this as a criterion to judge the contract's substantive adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinctive character of the administrative ('symbiotic') contract
rubrics_metrics.description: The concept of establishing this kind of a ‘symbiotic’ contract finds its purpose in being differentia specifica from any other contracts, thus having government on one side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate administrative contracts for features that distinguish them from ordinary private contracts (e.g., public-side participation, regulatory/monitoring requirements); the paper highlights uncertainty about how such agreements will be executed, monitored and regulated as part of that distinctiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative-novelty assessment
rubrics_metrics.description: Having in mind that such a contract represents a novelty here, but not in the European administrative space, it is our goal to determine and conclude whether this agreement provides an essence of citizens’ social and economic demands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use comparative analysis with European administrative practice to assess novelties introduced by the local Law on General Administrative Procedures; novelty on its own is not sufficient—assess practical implications, monitoring, and regulatory mechanisms.
